decided_by: the owner widened the selection before any labelling; rules written by Claude Code
source: MTSamples CSV (4,999 rows) at the owner's local path, outside the repository; note text never enters git. It has 29 Dermatology notes and 1 skin-pathology note, too few for the 50-note scoring minimum.

inclusion.skin_pathology: a pathology specialty and the text matches cdm.extract.SKIN
inclusion.specific_mention: any other specialty and the text matches cdm.extract.SPECIFIC: a skin-lesion diagnosis (melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, keratoacanthoma, nevus, seborrheic or actinic keratosis, dermatofibroma, cherry angioma, pyogenic granuloma, lentigo, skin cancer, pigmented lesion) or a skin biopsy, singular or plural
inclusion.generic_mention_only: any other specialty whose only match is cdm.extract.GENERIC ('skin lesion(s)', 'cutaneous lesion(s)'); many are review-of-systems lines such as 'no skin lesions', expected to have empty labels, which tests false positives. This is a pattern rule; the labels decide
inclusion.also_included: history-only and family-history mentions, and a few possibly non-skin uses (an oral or ocular nevus, a non-cutaneous melanoma): they are labelled as the note reads, usually 'not stated'
inclusion.excluded: incidental skin words, which the earlier SKIN pattern matched, and empty transcriptions; a text listed under several specialties counts once, under Dermatology where it is there

split.rule: notes ordered by note ID; within each selection group the first 10% (at least one) are development, the rest scoring; fixed before any prompt runs
split.why_stratified: an unstratified 10% put mostly generic mentions in development

superseded: two earlier sheets, never labelled, kept outside the repository: 30 notes (Dermatology and skin pathology, 20% development) and 73 notes (unstratified split)
